subject: Post-demo: model pathway, structured-output compliance & retry playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Hayes <rebecca.hayes@openhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model pathway, structured-output compliance & retry playbook

Hi Rebecca —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and an actionable next-step list so we can move to a pilot: 

1) What we heard you need
- High-precision structured extraction from clinical notes (JSON schema output for downstream ETL)
- Tool/function calling to enrich with patient-metadata lookups (safe, idempotent calls)
- Low-latency tails for the triage path, ability to trade cost/perf for bulk batch processing on nightly jobs
- Regression monitoring for quality when model or prompt changes are rolled

2) Model pathway we recommend (start -> pilot -> scale)
- Pilot: Optima-7B-q4f (fast, quantized; good balance for structured extraction and lower token cost)
- Production (tiered): Calliope-13B / Calliope-13B-rtc for low-latency route, fallback to Optima-7B for bulk jobs
- For hallucination-sensitive fields we recommend an n-best + confidence threshold policy with schema enforcement at the function-call layer

3) Structured output and retries (short checklist)
- Use a JSON schema to validate responses server-side (we can enable strict schema rejection or tolerant repair mode)
- Function calls: Redwood SDK supports function signatures and will only pass validated JSON to your downstream; it also provides explicit call metadata (request_id, model_variant, kv_cache-id) in the response for tracing
- Retry strategy: for non-idempotent tool-calls, we recommend at-most-once semantics using an external idempotency token per source record; for idempotent enrichment (lookups) we use exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 2s, 3 retries)

4) Benchmarks & artifacts attached/linked
- Attached: openhealth_promptset_v1.jsonl (sample prompts we discussed), benchmarks_openhealth_20280701.csv (latency/cost baseline from a similar customer), redwood_structured_output_playbook.pdf (implementation patterns)
- Links: shared benchmark sheet and structured-output docs: https://drive.google.com/openhealth-benchmarks-20280701, https://docs.redwood.ai/docs/structured-output-playbook

5) Proposed next steps
- You: share a small set (50–200) of anonymized clinical notes for a targeted extraction run (we can sign an addendum/NDA if needed)
- Us: run a 2-week pilot, deliver a report with schema pass-rate, false-positive/negative sampling, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens
- Commercial: Marissa will propose a pilot quote and procurement path after we confirm the sample data scope

If that all sounds right I can kick off the data ingestion checklist and schedule a pilot kickoff next week.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model pathway, structured-output compliance & retry playbook

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we share sample data: 

- JSON schema enforcement: does Redwood reject the response server-side and return a validation error, or do you offer an automated repair/transform option? We have strict downstream consumers so any silently malformed records are a problem.
- Tool/function calling idempotency: does the SDK generate idempotency tokens for each call or do we need to provide those? We expect some of our enrichment calls to be non-idempotent.
- Pilot pricing ballpark and SLA expectations (we'd like to understand latency SLOs for the triage route vs. nightly batch).

Looping in procurement on the pricing question. We'll also need a short NDA or data-processing addendum before sharing any clinical snippets.

—Rebecca
Head of Product, OpenHealth
rebecca.hayes@openhealth.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Hayes <rebecca.hayes@openhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model pathway, structured-output compliance & retry playbook

Hi Rebecca — quick answers inline, and I've attached the short tech note for deeper detail.

- JSON schema enforcement: we support three modes you can choose per-route: 1) strict-reject (Redwood returns a 422 with the validation error and does not forward the payload), 2) repair-suggest (we return the original plus a repair suggestion and confidence score), 3) tolerant (we forward with an audit flag). For OpenHealth I recommend strict-reject for critical fields and repair-suggest for peripheral fields so you don't lose throughput.

- Idempotency tokens & non-idempotent calls: Redwood will not auto-generate application-level idempotency tokens for you; we surface a field in the SDK to pass a client-provided idempotency key. For convenience we provide a helper in the SDK to create a deterministic token from record_id + route_name. Server-side we track request_ids and will de-dupe identical idempotency keys within a 24-hour window.

- Pilot pricing & SLAs: Marissa (cc'd) will provide a tailored pilot quote. For the triage low-latency route we can target a 99th pct latency SLO of 400ms on Calliope-13B-rtc with a production SLA on Dedicated; the Optima-7B pilot baseline typically sits at 120–200ms median and 700–900ms p99 depending on sequence length. Nightly batch jobs can be configured on reserved capacity for reduced unit price.

Next actions I propose:
- Marissa to share pilot quote and procurement steps
- Rebecca to send NDA request / DPA or confirm doc we should sign
- We draft a short mutual action plan and pilot success metrics (schema pass-rate >= 98%, precision recall targets for key fields)

Attaching: redwood_structured_output_playbook.pdf (see section 3.2 for enforcement modes)

Regards,
Karthik

Subject: Pilot proposal & procurement steps for OpenHealth

Hi Rebecca / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions and for the quick turnaround. Attached is a short pilot proposal and cost estimate based on the Optima-7B pilot scoping Karthik suggested. Highlights: 

- 2-week pilot: up to 200k input tokens processed; delivery includes schema pass-rate report, 100 sampled annotations with error taxonomy, latency/cost baseline, and a small recommendations playbook for production rollout.
- Pilot price (one-time): $12,500 (includes reserved pilot capacity + engineering support up to 20 hours)
- Optional add-ons: SOC2 evidence review ($3k), additional engineering hours ($320/hr)
- Commercial path: if pilot results meet success criteria we can convert to a 6/12-month reserved capacity commitment with predictable unit pricing and SLA.

Procurement: we can execute an NDA/DPA first. I can start the DocuSign if you confirm the signer and billing entity. DocuSign (example): https://app.docusign.com/example/ds-op-health-ndapa

Next steps (action owners)
- OpenHealth: confirm NDA signer & share anonymized sample (pointed to S3 presigned link or secure upload) — action: Rebecca
- Redwood: schedule kickoff call (post-NDA) and ingest pipeline checklist — action: Karthik
- Redwood/Finance: provide formal PO/invoice templates — action: Marissa

Happy to hop on a quick call to finalize — let me know availability this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
